title: 2002 AMC 12A Problem 25
statement: The nonzero coefficients of a polynomial \(P\) with real coefficients are all replaced by their mean to form a polynomial \(Q.\) Which of the following could be a graph of \(y = P(x)\) and \(y = Q(x)\) over the interval \(-4 \le x \le 4?\)

solutions.text:
Replacing the nonzero coefficients by their mean keeps the total of the coefficients unchanged, so \(P\) and \(Q\) have the same coefficient sum. Since \(P(1)\) and \(Q(1)\) each equal that sum, \(P(1) = Q(1).\)

Therefore the graphs of \(y = P(x)\) and \(y = Q(x)\) must cross at \(x = 1.\) The only choice showing an intersection at \(x = 1\) is graph B. (There, \(P(x) = 2x^4 - 3x^2 - 3x - 4\) and \(Q(x) = -2x^4 - 2x^2 - 2x - 2.\))

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The sum of the coefficients of \(P\) equals the sum of the coefficients of \(Q\)
Evaluating at \(x = 1\) gives \(P(1) = Q(1),\) so the two graphs must intersect at \(x = 1\)
